title: Mirabel and the Group Chat
premise: Wren Ashgrove, a seventeen-year-old coder who runs an anonymous account exposing her elite school's injustices, has spent fifteen years perfecting invisibility since the night she was placed with the Ashgroves. When the school's legendary ghost begins leaving notes addressed to 'Wren' in ink that shouldn't exist, she realizes someone knows both identities — and is forcing her toward confession. As the notes escalate and her best friend Priya's final audition collides with Wren's biggest exposé yet, Wren must choose between protecting her secret inheritance of silence or claiming her real name. In the end, she reveals herself publicly at the audition, loses Priya's trust temporarily but gains a chosen family — including the ghost, who turns out to be the school's oldest caretaker guarding letters from every forgotten kid who came before her.
about_author: S. M. Galloway is a former school archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the marginalia students left behind in library books. They write stories about kids who speak in code — literal and otherwise — and live in a drafty house full of unlabeled boxes.

chapters.title: The Account That Knows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We meet @hollowoak_truths, Wren's anonymous exposé account, as it drops its most dangerous post yet about the school's scholarship fund skimming. Establish her careful double life: flawless student by day, ghost by night. Emotional beat: the thrill of justice shadowed by terror of being known.

chapters.title: Impossible Ink
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A note appears inside her locker: 'Hello, Wren Ashgrove' — written in ink that shifts color and can't be photographed. No one uses her birth surname. She tests the ink scientifically and fails. Emotional beat: the first crack in fifteen years of control.

chapters.title: Priya's Audition Season
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya prepares for the conservatory's final audition while navigating their friendship, unaware of Wren's account. She notices Wren flinching at her own name. Emotional beat: warmth and the ache of loving someone who won't let you all the way in.

chapters.title: Rules of Being Invisible
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback woven through present: how eight-year-old Wren learned that names get you hurt, and how the Ashgroves' kindness came with unspoken conditions. The ghost leaves a second note quoting something only child-Wren ever said aloud. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing.

chapters.title: The Group Chat
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs via chat logs. The friend group's chat becomes a character itself — jokes, coded warnings, and Priya defending an anonymous poster Wren secretly is. The ghost starts replying inside the chat from an account that shouldn't exist. Emotional beat: belonging that feels borrowed.

chapters.title: Hollow Oak Lore
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren researches the school ghost, Hollow Oak's 'Inkwell,' said to write letters for students the school failed. She finds a 1970s letter in the archive signed with shifting ink. Emotional beat: hope disguised as skepticism.

chapters.title: What the Fund Bought
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Her investigation deepens: the skimmed scholarship money traces to a trustee connected to her own adoption paperwork. The stakes turn personal. A third note says: 'They took your name. I kept it.' Emotional beat: rage finding a target.

chapters.title: Almost Telling Priya
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A late-night rehearsal; Priya almost confesses her own secret (she's terrified of failing, of being a charity case) but Wren deflects with a joke. Both girls go home lonely. Emotional beat: parallel silences.

chapters.title: The Trustee's Daughter
chapters.summary: New POV: Marisol, trustee's daughter and group chat member, discovers her father's ledger and panics. She suspects @hollowoak_truths knows. She starts quietly testing her friends' loyalties. Emotional beat: fear wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Ink Under Ultraviolet
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finally photographs the ink under UV: hidden beneath each note is a date and a name — other students, decades apart, all scholarship kids erased from records. The ghost isn't haunting her; it's recruiting her. Emotional beat: awe tipping into obligation.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Archive
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren breaks into the archive at night and meets the ghost: Mr. Okafor, the caretaker, keeper of forty years of confiscated letters. He explains the ink — made from oak gall and ash — and why he chose her. Emotional beat: being seen for the first time.

chapters.title: The Condition
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. He offers Wren the archive — the proof, the names, the inheritance of every silenced kid — on one condition: she must publish under her true name, not the anonymous handle. She refuses and storms out. Emotional beat: pride colliding with purpose.

chapters.title: Marisol Closes In
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol narrows the suspect list to three friends and plants a false story in the group chat. Wren takes the bait, nearly exposing herself. Emotional beat: paranoia poisoning intimacy.

chapters.title: Audition Week Begins
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Audition week; Priya's nerves fray as Wren keeps vanishing. Marisol hints to Priya that someone in the chat has been lying to them all. Emotional beat: trust beginning to tilt.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Marisol leaks Wren's draft exposé to the administration, stripped of attribution but timestamped from Wren's device. Wren faces suspension unless she names her source — Okafor. Emotional beat: cornered.

chapters.title: What Silence Costs
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Offered immunity if she betrays Okafor, Wren almost signs. Then she reads one of the archived letters — from a girl in 1983 who was expelled for telling the truth. Emotional beat: the inheritance finally understood.

chapters.title: Priya Finds Out
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers Wren is @hollowoak_truths — and that Wren let Priya defend the account without knowing. The fight is quiet and devastating: 'You let me love a stranger.' Emotional beat: betrayal before the audition.

chapters.title: The Final Audition
chapters.summary: Alternating Wren/Priya POV. Priya performs brilliantly, hollow-eyed. Wren waits in the wings holding two statements: the retraction she was offered, and the truth. Emotional beat: the held breath before the leap.

chapters.title: Wren Ashgrove, By Name
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Climax: instead of retracting, Wren publishes the full exposé under her real name, live during the audition reception, naming the trustee, the fund, and herself. Chaos, cameras, Marisol's choice to hand over the ledger. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into freedom.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Shifting Ink
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Consequences land: the trustee resigns, Wren faces discipline but the student body rallies, and Priya doesn't speak to her. Okafor gives Wren the archive key anyway — she earned it by paying the price. Emotional beat: victory with a hole in it.

chapters.title: Letters to the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Okafor digitize the archive so no name gets lost again. She writes her own letter for the collection — addressed to the girl she used to be. Emotional beat: mourning and integration.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Priya's POV, closing. Weeks later, Priya finds Wren's letter in the archive and finally understands the whole shape of her friend's silence. She leaves a note in shifting ink of her own: 'Encore?' On the walk home, they meet halfway. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a chosen belonging.
